 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.01.2023. 
Chikkarevanna vs Jiji .P.C on 1 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162631786/
1 2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 17.01.2023 at about 01.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA41EG 7686 towards Kumbalagudu to Rajarajeshwari Dental college,
while taking uturn at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KL46V7327 drove the same very fast SCCH4 3 MVC No.843/2023 and negligently and hit the petitioner's motorcycle, due to the impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries on his right leg and other parts of the body. 
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and he has spent huge amount towards medicine, nourishment, transportation and conveyance etc.,.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as security guard and he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest. 
SCCH4 4 MVC No.843/2023 3. The respondent No.1 and 2 have entered appearance through their advocates and filed their respective objection statements separately. 
The respondent No.1 in his written statement contending that he is the RC owner of Car baring Reg.
No. KL46V7327 and it has insured with second respondent. Further, denied the involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident. 
The respondent No.2 in his written statement has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of first respondent in respect of offending Car and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further contended that, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties, as the owner and insurer of the motorcycle were not made as parties to the proceedings. Further denies the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident. Further SCCH4 5 MVC No.843/2023 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the petitioner suddenly tried to u turn as such the petitioner has attributed sole negligence for causing the accident. There was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Car. The petitioner riding the motorcycle without having DL, not wearing safety helmet and thus the petitioner being guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and regulations, he is not entitled for any compensation. 
Further both the respondents denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with cost. 
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues arise for my consideration:
Chikkarevanna vs Jiji .P.C on 1 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162631786/
2 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving SCCH4 6 MVC No.843/2023 of Car bearing Reg.No.KA46V7327 by its driver in RTA took place on 17.01.2023 at about 1.45 p.m., on Kumbalagudu Police station Uturn, near Ramohalli Cross, Kumbalagudu kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru? 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award? 
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 16. Further, one witness is examined as PW.2, through his got marked documents at Ex.P.17 and 18. Inspite of given sufficient opportunity the respondents did not adduce evidence. 
6. I have heard the counsel for both the parties. 
7. My findings on the above issues are as under. 
Issue No.1 : Partly in the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative ,
 Issue No.3 : As per the final orders  for the following:
 SCCH4 7 MVC No.843/2023  : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8. That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of chiefexamination which is considered as P.W.1. In support of his case, he has produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, charge sheet, spot Mahazar, IMV Report, Wound Certificate and Certificate u/s 65(b) of evidence Act. All these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9. On going through the documents one Revana siddaiah has lodged complaint with Kumbalagodu Police station in Ramanagara district, on 17.01.2023, alleging that, on the same day at about 1.45 p.m., while the complainant was driving the vehicle bearing No. KA41 EG7686 and while taking Uturn, on BangaloreMysore road, by that time, the driver of Maruthi suzuki car bearing Reg. No.
KL46V7327 came in rash and negligent manner with high speed and hit the petitioner's SCCH 4 8 MVC No.843/2023 vehicle, due to which the petitioner sustained fracture injury on his right leg and other parts of the body. After the accident petitioner was shifted to nearest Rajarajeshwari Chikkarevanna vs Jiji .P.C on 1 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162631786/
3 Hospital.
10. On the basis of complaint, police have registered FIR against the driver of the car referred in the complaint. After registering FIR police have visited the place of accident and also drawn spot mahazar and also taken photographs of vehicles involved in the accident. The damages caused to both the vehicles involved in the accident are also noted in the IMV Report. As per Wound Certificate, the petitioner has taken treatment immediately after the accident at Rajarajeshwari medical college and hospital. In the Wound certificate it is also noted that, right leg fracture. The Police after completion of investigation laid charge sheet against Jenil.PJ for offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of SCCH4 9 MVC No.843/2023 IPC. The allegations made in the complaint as well as charge sheet are one and the same. 
11. The respondent No.1 has filed written statement and admitted the accident. The second respondent in the written statement has taken up defense that, there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Car, the petitioner riding the motorcycle without having Driving License and not waring safety helmet, the petitioner being guilty of violation of motor vehicles rules, he is not entitled for compensation. Further, it is also contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner who suddenly tried to take Uturn, that means the second respondent do not dispute the accident except the negligence. During the course of crossexamination of PW.1, nothing worth is being elicited so as to prove the negligence on the part of the petitioner, the second SCCH4 10 MVC No.843/2023 respondent has not adduced rebuttal evidence. During the course of crossexamination of petitioner, it has been suggested that, petitioner ought to have cross the road after passing of the vehicles coming from opposite side, but the alleged offending car came from right side of the petitioner and hit the petitioner's vehicle, while the driver of the alleged offending car proceeding on the high way, he ought to have taken more caution. Like wise the petitioner while taking U turn it was his duty look after the vehicles which were coming in the main road. Looking to the facts of the case and damages caused to both the vehicle involved in the accident the accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner and rider of the offending vehicle. However, there is no specific formula to ascertain the exact percentage of negligence of both the persons. Taking in to consideration of fact and circumstance of the case I hold that petitioner has also contributed 50%
negligence and remaining negligence is SCCH4 11 MVC No.843/2023 on the part of driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KL46V 7327 which belonging to respondent No.1. Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 partly in the affirmative. 
ISSUE No.2:
12. As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle of respondent. Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation. Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads. 
13. To prove the nature of his injuries the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2, though him, Clinical Notes and Xrays which are marked under Ex.P.17 and 18. As per the evidence of PW2, the petitioner has sustained closed Chikkarevanna vs Jiji .P.C on 1 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162631786/
4 fracture of the right femur, closed right ankle bimalleloar fracture and closed comminuted fracture of the right distal ulna. Further SCCH4 12 MVC No.843/2023 PW.2 deposed that, total disability of right lower limb at 56%, right upper limb at 32% and that of his whole body at 23%. 
14. According to the evidence of PW.2 the petitioner need another surgery for removal of implant and the estimate of the surgery is around Rs.90,000/. Hence, it can be considered that the petitioner is required at least Rs.60,000/ for future medical expenses. 
15. According to the petitioner prior to the accident he was working as security guard in Rajarajeshwari Dental College and he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month. The disability caused to the petitioner would affect on his avocation. Considering this fact, I hold that the petitioner has sustained 23% permanent physical and avocational disability. 
16. In this regard the petitioner has not produced any documents. In the absence of proof of income the SCCH4 13 MVC No.843/2023 notional income of the petitioner in the year2023 may be considered at Rs.16,000/, in the year2023, then one day wages would Rs.533/. 
17. As per discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.15, the petitioner was admitted to hospital as an inpatient from 17.01.2023 to 21.01.2023 and again from 27.06.2023 to 01.07.2023 i.e., for total 09 days, after discharge from the hospital there was need of rest at least for 21 days. So, the petitioner is entitled compensation of Rs.31,980/ (30 days X Rs.533/ = 15,990/) during the laid up period with one attendant charge at the same rate. 
18. As per the medical bills produced at Ex.P.9, 12 and 16 the petitioner has spent Rs.1,21,920/.
This medical bills are not disproved. So the petitioner is entitled for the same. 
SCCH4 14 MVC No.843/2023 19. As mentioned in petition as on the date of accident the age of petitioner was 46 years. In this regard the petitioner has produced Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P8. As per these documents the date of birth of the petitioner is 30.01.1977 and the accident took place in the year 2023. So, as on the date of the accident, the petitioner was aged about 46 years. 
20. As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '13'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/ X 12 X 13 X 23% =Rs.5,74,080/
which is the total loss of future income. 
21. Hence, I inclined to award the compensation to the petitioner under the following heads:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 5,74,080/
2. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 31,980/ up period and attendant charge.
3. Conveyance charges Rs. 20,000/ SCCH4 15 MVC No.843/2023 Chikkarevanna vs Jiji .P.C on 1 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162631786/
5 4. Pain, sufferings and loss of Rs. 1,20,000 / amenities 5. Food nourishment, attendant Rs. 60,000/ charges and loss of amenities 6. Medical bills Rs. 1,21,920/
7. Future medical bills Rs. 60,000/ Total Rs. 9,87,980/
22. As already held above, the petitioner has also contributed negligence at 50%, hence he is not entitle for compensation to that extent which comes to Rs. 4,93,990/ The petitioner is entitled for compensation to the extent of 50% which comes to Rs.4,93,990/.
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle. But the second respondent has denied the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle. As per the photo state copy of the insurance policy produced by petitioner, the second respondent has issued policy to the offending vehicle, in SCCH4 16 MVC No.843/2023 the name of first respondent, which was inforce as on the date of the accident. Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation behalf of the respondent No.1 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative. 
ISSUE NO.4:
23. For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost. 
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,93,990/ (Rupees four lakh ninety three thousand nine hundred and ninety only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
SCCH4 17 MVC No.843/2023 The respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order. 
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour. 
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/.
Draw up award accordingly.

summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.01.2023.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Medical Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and he has spent huge amount towards medicine, nourishment, transportation and conveyance etc.,.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as security guard and he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest.

The respondent No.1 in his written statement contending that he is the RC owner of Car baring Reg.
No. KL46V7327 and it has insured with second respondent.
Further, denied the involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident.
The respondent No.2 in his written statement has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of first respondent in respect of offending Car and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties, as the owner and insurer of the motorcycle were not made as parties to the proceedings.
Further SCCH4 5 MVC No.843/2023 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the petitioner suddenly tried to u turn as such the petitioner has attributed sole negligence for causing the accident.
There was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Car.
The petitioner riding the motorcycle without having DL, not wearing safety helmet and thus the petitioner being guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and regulations, he is not entitled for any compensation.

Further both the respondents denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive.

summary.ANALYSIS:
The second respondent in the written statement has taken up defense that, there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Car, the petitioner riding the motorcycle without having Driving License and not waring safety helmet, the petitioner being guilty of violation of motor vehicles rules, he is not entitled for compensation.
During the course of crossexamination of PW.1, nothing worth is being elicited so as to prove the negligence on the part of the petitioner, the second SCCH4 10 MVC No.843/2023 respondent has not adduced rebuttal evidence.
Looking to the facts of the case and damages caused to both the vehicle involved in the accident the accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner and rider of the offending vehicle.
However, there is no specific formula to ascertain the exact percentage of negligence of both the persons.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.

Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
